faqs.question: When is an employer legally required to constitute an Internal Committee (IC)?
faqs.answer: Under Section 4(1) of the POSH Act 2013, every employer employing 10 or more employees (including permanent, contractual, ad-hoc, and interns) across any branch or administrative unit is statutorily required to constitute an Internal Committee. Failure to constitute an IC attracts penalties up to ₹50,000 under Section 26(1), with repeated non-compliance risking cancellation of corporate registration or operating licenses.

faqs.question: What are the legal qualifications for the External Member on the Internal Committee?
faqs.answer: Section 4(2)(c) of the POSH Act requires the appointment of at least one member from an NGO or association committed to the cause of women, or a person familiar with issues relating to sexual harassment, such as an experienced advocate. The External Member ensures institutional neutrality, adheres strictly to principles of natural justice, and prevents management bias.

faqs.question: How should cross-border or interstate dispute resolution clauses be drafted in commercial agreements?
faqs.answer: Commercial agreements should explicitly specify: (1) Governing law (e.g., Laws of India), (2) Mode of resolution (e.g., Arbitration under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act 1996), (3) Seat and venue (e.g., Kolkata, West Bengal), and (4) Institutional administration rules. Clear seat designation avoids conflicting jurisdictional challenges before state High Courts.

faqs.question: What is the procedure for seeking urgent interim relief before the Calcutta High Court?
faqs.answer: Urgent interim relief (such as ad-interim injunctions or stay orders) is sought by filing a petition before the appropriate bench (Original or Appellate Side). Matters involving acute commercial urgency can be listed via urgent mentioning before the Hon'ble Court with advance notice served upon the caveator or opposing parties as per Calcutta High Court Rules.

faqs.question: What is the statutory limitation period for conducting an inquiry under the POSH Act?
faqs.answer: Under Section 11(4) of the Act, an inquiry into a complaint must be completed within 90 days. Within 10 days of completing the inquiry, the committee must provide its findings report to the employer. The employer is then obligated under Section 13(4) to implement the recommendations within 60 days.
